_about: Stop order as the dispatchers actually left it in ePASS Routing, transcribed from Cayden's 9/17 screenshots.
Each tech-day in ePASS is a sequence with a comment row in it — usually literally 'routed', once 'routed?',
once 'keep at 5'. Everything ABOVE the comment is the route, in driving order. Everything BELOW it is a
ticket dated that day that is not being driven to: the tech has to go back into it and update the status
(a part that came in, an SO6 that needs re-booking, an SO8 waiting to post). That divider is the field
reality behind spec item 'needs tech input'. A day can also be blocked with a 24-unit comment ('BLL is off').
The invoice export carries no sequence, so this file is the only source of order; days without a
screenshot fall back to the engine's ZIP order and say so.

epass_map_summary_2026-09-18._note: ePASS Dispatching Map route table for 9/18 — its 'Job' column is a flat 30 minutes per UNIT, not a per-job estimate: CEM has 5 stops but two of them are 2-unit tickets, 7 units = 3:30. Units is the only duration signal ePASS has; our duration table (§4.4) is per category and install type.
